## TL;DR

The review (pass 8, "needs some work") named five bug classes in the close-out progress feature. The fixes are in the recorder, the job coordinator, the remote runner and the pipeline label, and retries now get their own attempt and log. The drawer shot declares step, host and attempt. The local scoped check passed earlier. The remote gate stopped on a WebKit perf budget once and on a server-side finalization timeout since, and the draft has gone missing from the worktree more than once.

## Work and rationale

- **Heartbeats emit a snapshot.** `CloseOutProgressRecorder` calls `onChange` after every persisted write, heartbeats included, so the card and drawer see a live `lastProgressAt` during a quiet sync or publish instead of a false stall.
- **Failed writes are retried, not dropped.** A log line or job-record write that does not land is kept and sent with the next write. `lastProgressAt` moves only when the log line landed. Pending lines are capped at 100.
- **Staleness is judged on the recorder alone.** `buildIntegrationSnapshot` checks `progressIsStale` against the attempt's own timestamp, so fresh stage events cannot mask a recorder that stopped writing.
- **Host-slot wait is visible.** The Tailscale pool loop reports `queued` from `onQueue` and `acquired` with the host once it holds a slot. The orchestrator maps these to "queued for host slot" and "remote validation".
- **Remote build is not labelled as tests.** The combined `run` stage maps to "remote validation". `ActiveRemoteRunRegistry.setTestProgress` moves the run to `test` on its first test marker.
- **Retries are new attempts.** `advanceAttempt` writes a new generation, sets `previousFailure` to the failure that caused it, and clears step, host and progress. The recorder's `beginAttempt` moves the log and records the reason on both logs. Gate reruns and host failover both use this path. A cancelled record is never advanced.
- **Stalled labels keep context.** The label names the step it stopped on and the retry reason, on both card and drawer.
- **Fixture.** `drawer:closeOutRemoteTests` carries step "running tests (27/84)", host "bee", attempt 2, and a previous failure.

## Approaches tried

I first planned a separate `renewAttempt` method. The committed work already had `advanceAttempt` on the same record with the same fencing, so I kept it. I also considered judging staleness from the newest of stage events and recorder writes, which is what the review flagged, so staleness uses the recorder only.

## Challenges and blockers

- **Worktree lock.** While each handoff check ran, RepoOS made the `src/` files read-only. I did not override the lock. An early handoff failed because my edits changed the tree mid-check.
- **Concurrent checkpoints.** WIP checkpoint commits from an earlier engineer turn (08:44–08:59) were already in the worktree. I verified them against the review findings and built on them.
- **Server timeouts.** A handoff ran about 15 minutes and failed with "server-side finalization timed out". I cannot fix that from the branch.
- **Perf budget on the remote runner.** The WebKit work-board test at 375px on bee failed its timing budget. It passes locally (3/3 in 38 seconds), and the work-board code is not in this change, so I read it as runner load. I did not loosen the budget.
- **Missing report draft.** The handoff failed at review because `.repoos/engineering-report-drafts/1276.md` was absent from the worktree. The draft has been rewritten each time it went missing.

## Key learnings

- A handoff request from a linked worktree may not reach the server board. The activity log is the reliable check.
- Edits during a running check are unsafe even when the check does not read them.
- A timing-sensitive browser test can fail on a loaded runner where it passes on an idle machine. Check whether the failing test covers the changed code before treating the failure as real.
